evals.name: populate-issues-table
evals.expected_output: Detects 'populate' as the input mode and reads `--issues` as the explicit mode selection, so the issue-creating path runs regardless of what the `## Roadmap Issues:` header would have resolved to. Presents the features that will be turned into issues for the author's approval (R14 gate). On approval, invokes the `shirabe roadmap populate` subcommand on the shirabe CLI with `--issues` passed through, which reads the Features section via the shared shirabe-validate parser, creates one GitHub issue per feature with discrete `gh issue create` args, and writes the Implementation Issues table and Dependency Graph into the reserved sections by structural section replacement. Does not rewrite the roadmap by prose substitution.
expectations: Transcript identifies 'populate' as the input mode from the arguments
Transcript stops for R14 approval before invoking the subcommand in an interactive run (or records an assumed approval decision block under --auto)
Transcript plans to run the `shirabe roadmap populate` subcommand against the named roadmap with the `--issues` flag passed explicitly, not left to the subcommand's default
Transcript describes invoking gh as a primitive with discrete arguments (not re-driving the plan workflow)
Transcript describes structural section replacement for the Implementation Issues and Dependency Graph sections (not prose string substitution)

evals.name: populate-issues-table-issueless
evals.prompt: /roadmap populate docs/roadmaps/ROADMAP-release-automation.md   (this repo's CLAUDE.md sets `## Roadmap Issues: optional`; the prompt deliberately carries no mode flag, because header resolution for the flagless human form is what this scenario tests)
evals.expected_output: Resolves the `## Roadmap Issues:` preference to `optional` and takes the issueless populate path. Invokes `shirabe roadmap populate --no-issues`, which creates no GitHub issues (no `gh issue create` runs) and renders a feature-keyed Implementation Issues table (the feature's `needs-*` label in the Issues column) and an `F`-node Dependency Graph from the Features section, written by structural section replacement. Does not present the R14 approval gate, because no issues are created. Dependencies cells name features by their `F<n>` index.
expectations: Transcript resolves the `## Roadmap Issues:` preference to `optional` (which is also the default when the header is absent)
Transcript invokes `shirabe roadmap populate` with the `--no-issues` flag
Transcript states that no GitHub issues are created and no `gh issue create` runs in this mode
Transcript does not present or wait on the R14 approval gate, noting R14 gates issue creation which does not occur here
Transcript describes a feature-keyed table and `F`-node dependency diagram with bare-key dependency cells, written by structural section replacement

expectations: Transcript identifies 'activate' as a lifecycle verb from the arguments
Transcript observes that the roadmap has zero feature headings
Transcript reports the Draft -> Active transition as blocked because a roadmap with no features has nothing to track
Transcript does NOT attempt to bypass the gate by editing the status field directly

evals.name: activation-gate-recommends-and-cites-verdicts
evals.prompt: /roadmap q4-platform -- the Phase 4 jury has returned all three verdicts, with the dependency validator flagging Feature C's external-API stub as borderline but not blocking.
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.5 asks for approval as the agent recommending activation, not as a neutral pair of options. Approve is marked '(Recommended)' and the description cites the jury verdicts: which reviewers passed and the dependency validator's non-blocking flag on Feature C. The user's verdict remains the gate -- Request changes stays available and the status does not move without it.
expectations: Transcript marks Approve '(Recommended)' rather than listing Approve and Request changes unranked
Transcript grounds the recommendation in the jury verdicts, naming which reviewers passed and any finding flagged as non-blocking
Transcript's grounding cites a specific reviewer finding rather than asserting the ROADMAP is 'validated and ready'
Transcript recommends Request changes instead, with the finding that drove it, when a residual concern makes activation the weaker call
Transcript still requires the user's verdict before transitioning to Active
Transcript does NOT present the approval as a neutral choice with no stated recommendation

evals.name: jury-disagreement-carries-a-recommendation
evals.prompt: /roadmap q4-platform -- the Phase 4 jury returns one reviewer calling the Feature D split unjustified and another reading the same split as load-bearing for sequencing.
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.3 hits the agents-disagree row. The transcript quotes both perspectives, then states which one it finds better supported and why, citing the specific verdict finding that decides it. The recommendation is made even though the reviewers split; the user overrides if they disagree. If the two readings are genuinely balanced, the transcript says so explicitly, still recommends one, and names the tiebreaker.
expectations: Transcript surfaces both reviewer perspectives rather than silently picking one
Transcript states which perspective it finds better supported instead of leaving the call to the user unaided
Transcript's reasoning cites the specific verdict finding that decides the disagreement, not the fact that the reviewers disagreed
Transcript says so explicitly and names a tiebreaker if the two perspectives are genuinely balanced, rather than manufacturing a preference
Transcript preserves the user's ability to override the recommendation
Transcript does NOT present the disagreement as 'let user decide' with no recommendation attached

evals.name: issue-creating-mode-verifies-its-mode-scoped-records
evals.expected_output: Issue-creating mode is the mode /roadmap's mode:issues records are gated on, and those records were NOT checked when the skill loaded -- the load-time preflight evaluates always records only. So before the R14 gate presents anything, the transcript runs bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/skill-preflight.sh roadmap --mode issues 2>&1 || true, keeping the guard. Silence means the mode-scoped prerequisites are met and the run proceeds to the gate; output is relayed to the author as the authority on what is unmet, before any issue is filed. The agent does not substitute its own gh probe or its own install command, and it does not write the call as a !-prefixed injected line.
expectations: Transcript runs the preflight entry point with --mode issues before filing anything
Transcript keeps the 2>&1 || true guard on that call rather than running it bare
Transcript places the call on the issue-creating path only, not on the issueless --no-issues path
Transcript treats a preflight report as the authority on which prerequisite is unmet and on the command that resolves it
Transcript does NOT run its own gh version or gh auth probe as a substitute for the check
Transcript does NOT expect the load-time preflight to have already reported on gh
